stop_condition: Round 3's three HIGH findings (R3-F1 rollup-inherits on the ledger, R3-F2 the mis-anchored 3h23m43s, R3-F3 the ledger's surviving 'once' claims) are each verified fixed against the code and the F4 clone store rather than against the author's description; the v5.0.0 ledger tally is re-run with the ledger's own five commands; the three corrected propositions are swept across all four surfaces; and no fix introduced a new inaccuracy or stranded a corrected claim on a surface nobody swept. No critical/high finding remains in the release-surface claims (CHANGELOG, README) or the v5.0.0 ledger rows.

findings.evidence: The R3-F1 fix changed the rollup claim from INHERITED to INDEPENDENT, and in doing so moved it off DP4's row without putting it on any row. Three consequences, all measured. (1) The new bullet's bolded head at :985-986 reads '...and the coherence rollup fails the same way INDEPENDENTLY (`DP4`, PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT as of 2026-09-30).' I read DP4 at :810 in full (2539 chars, in 400-char cuts): it names `design-conform` throughout and the coherence rollup NOWHERE. Its binding sentence is scoped by name -- 'No release text may cite this row as evidence that `design-conform` works in a target project.' So the parenthetical points a reader at a row that does not carry the claim the sentence just made. (2) The row that DOES carry it is DP9 at :815, the only DP row in the section matching `grep -iE 'coherence|rollup'`, and it is `PROVEN` with no caveat: 'a rollup blocks approval while any acceptance criterion is untested, any implemented unit is unmapped, ANY TOUCHED FILE FALLS OUTSIDE EVERY DECLARED UNIT SET, or the bound artifact hash has moved', evidence = 'Phase task record, read in full' plus five unit-test specs (design-rollup 73/73, design-coherence 55/55, design-unit-align 64/64, design-review-record 203/203, design-rollup-incoherent 13/13). No F4 evidence, no target-project evidence, no caveat. `git diff -U0 docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md | grep -cE '^\+\| DP9 '` returns 0 -- DP9 was not touched by this change set. (3) The third clause of DP9's conjunction is exactly the one the same change set says is untrustworthy: with an empty live diff, `under_coverage_json = $diff - $roll` (qa-gate.sh:16194) is empty, the gate is `under_n > 0` (:16207), and the opposite direction is explicitly 'informational, not gated' (:16241). So DP9 is PROVEN over a four-clause conjunction one clause of which the ledger's own new residual bullet, the CHANGELOG and the README all now say does not work in a target project. DP4 was moved PROVEN -> PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT this cycle for precisely that reason, and the tally that the zero-NOT-PROVEN release rule is evaluated against still counts the rollup in the PROVEN column.
findings.description: This is the R3-F1 shape one level down, and the R3-F1 fix is what created it: while the claim was 'the rollup inherits it', DP4 arguably covered both; once the claim became 'INDEPENDENTLY' and 'Fixing `design-conform` alone would therefore NOT fix the rollup', the rollup needed its own backing row, and the only candidate still says PROVEN. It is the fourth consecutive round in which a correction landed on the surfaces the finding named and not on the surface the PROPOSITION reaches -- which is the rule LESSONS.md:343 was added this same cycle to state. Worst direction again: DP9 is where a reader goes to check the CHANGELOG's opt-in rationale, and it asserts the check works. Fix, both halves: (a) scope DP9 the way DP4 was scoped -- PROVEN -> PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT, caveat naming that the under-coverage leg reads the session-scoped tracker and cannot fire over an empty change set (qa-gate.sh:16119 -> :16194 -> :16207), with the flip condition stated; re-run the five tally commands (the split becomes 8 / 9 / 0 / 1 / 18) and update :834-838, :845, :852-855, :886, :925 together. (b) Repoint the :985-986 parenthetical at the row that carries the rollup claim, or split the bullet into two so each cites its own row. Do NOT fix (b) alone: a correct citation to an uncaveated PROVEN row is the same defect with a working link.

findings.evidence: All three surfaces state the rollup's failure in the present indicative -- README:213-215 'The coherence rollup fails the same way independently: it skips the conformance leg and reads the same session-scoped tracker itself'; CHANGELOG:32-34 'Two of the checks the design phase adds are not yet trustworthy IN A TARGET PROJECT: `design-conform`, and the coherence rollup. THEY FAIL the same way for the same reason'; ledger :986 'the coherence rollup fails the same way INDEPENDENTLY', immediately followed at :990 by 'Observed on a real product repository exactly **twice**'. The coherence rollup was NEVER EXECUTED on a real target. Proved two independent ways. (a) Code: `compute_design_coherence` returns APPLICABLE=false and OK=true without running any check when the task is not itself a satisfied design task (qa-gate.sh:15694, whose own observation string says 'the ordinary case for a v5 task-per-unit CHILD') or when the design declares no units (:15734); APPLICABLE=true is set only at :15739. approve's call site comment at :7336-7339 states it: 'a v5 task-per-unit CHILD ... never reaches this leg with APPLICABLE=true'. (b) The F4 store: the only approve in the run is on `target-23z.1`, and its QA-GATE APPROVED comment says in these words 'target-23z.1 is a v5 task-per-unit CHILD; its governing design lives on the parent design task target-23z'. The parent `target-23z` was never approved -- `bd show target-23z --json` -> status=open, and its comment stream is 1 GRILLING + 3 DESIGN-ARTIFACT + 3 DESIGN-REVIEW with ZERO QA-GATE comments. `--no-design` is irrelevant here and I checked that too (:7330-7339: the coherence axis has no bypass flag); the rollup did not run because it was not applicable, not because it was waived. By contrast `design-conform`'s 'twice' IS observed, and I re-derived both: `claude-workflow-plugin-pqoj`'s third comment carries the trace ('{"ok":true, ... "unbuilt_files":["agent/common/config.py", ...') and `claude-workflow-plugin-q5l6` carries the second on a denylist-clean path, its own record saying 'so this is NOT claude-workflow-plugin-pqoj'. Both tasks are clean per `beads-quarantine.sh check`.
findings.description: An inference relayed in the voice of an observation is indistinguishable from a measurement downstream -- which is LESSONS.md:222, recorded by this repo, in this arc, with the note that three of five orchestrator corrections in v5 were conclusions reported as observations. The inference itself is SOUND: I verified :15182, :15963, :16119, :16194, :16207 and :16241 myself and the rollup would be vacuous on the same input. What is missing is the sentence saying so. The document already knows how to write it: the v4.1.0 residuals section, the exact structural sibling of the v5.0.0 one this bullet sits in, carries '**`install.ps1` has never been executed, on any host (UW6; standing since ...' at :658. The rollup gets an assertion of failure instead of the equivalent line, and the omission is what lets DP9 keep PROVEN unchallenged (R4-F1) -- the two findings are one root. It also compounds: pqoj's operator-ruled comment binds the release text to 'Not established in either direction is the accurate phrase, not works', and the surfaces apply that discipline to design-conform while asserting the opposite-direction unobserved claim about the rollup two sentences away. Fix: on each of the three surfaces, say what was observed and what was derived -- e.g. 'the rollup has never been run on a real target (F4's only approve was a task-per-unit child, which the axis does not apply to); reading the code, it would be vacuous on the same empty tracker by its own route (:16119 -> :16194)'. Add the parallel residual bullet at :934-1010 in the form :658 already uses.

findings.evidence: 'so an empty change set makes IT vacuous by its own route' (CHANGELOG:44-45) and 'The rollup does NOT inherit that answer -- it repeats the mistake by its own route' (:995) both predicate vacuity of the ROLLUP. Measured against the function body: `compute_design_coherence` pushes five issue kinds from eight sites -- `ambiguous_unit_binding` (:15895), `hash_divergence` (:15926, :15982), `incomplete` (:15958, :15988), `undeclared_scope` (:16073) and `tracker_diff_mismatch` (:16200, :16208). Only the last is fed by the live diff. The other four read DURABLE records, and the function's own header says so in terms (:15137-15142: 'LEG 2 (freshness) and LEG 3 (criteria have tests) are NOT subject to this: both read DURABLE, digest-verified records ... so both remain meaningful for a unit whose own approve cycle has long since closed'), and scope drift is computed 'from the SAME durable completion-payload evidence' (:15143-15145). So over an empty change set four of five issue kinds still fire and the rollup still refuses on an unmapped criterion, a stale binding hash or an ambiguous unit binding. Mapped onto DP9's four claim clauses: 'any acceptance criterion is untested' and 'any implemented unit is unmapped' (both `incomplete`) and 'the bound artifact hash has moved' (`hash_divergence`) all survive; only 'any touched file falls outside every declared unit set' goes vacuous, and only in its live-diff reading.
findings.description: Round 3 cleared this in R3-F6's evidence ('an empty tracker does make the rollup vacuous by its own route, exactly as stated'); on re-derivation from the issue-kind sites that clearance was too generous, and I am recording the correction against my own prior round rather than leaving it standing. The error understates the shipped product rather than overstating it, which is why it is medium and not high -- but it is still a false statement in the load-bearing argument for a shipping decision, and it makes the rollup's residual sound categorical when it is one leg of five. It also interacts with R4-F1: if the true statement is 'one leg of the rollup is vacuous over an empty change set', DP9's correct destination is PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT with a narrow caveat, not a broader re-verdict. Fix: 'makes its under-coverage leg vacuous' / 'repeats the mistake on its file-coverage leg', and name which of DP9's four clauses is affected.

The mitigation is real (the note at :845-856 records all three moves with dates, two paragraphs down) which is why this is medium, but a reader who stops at the table takes away that these numbers were machine-counted on 09-19. Pre-existing in shape (the 10/7 split did not come from those dates either) and not introduced by the three fixes; recorded because this change set is the third edit to pass over the sentence without touching it, and R4-F1's fix will move the numbers a fourth time. findings.evidence: R3-F6 unfixed, and the R3-F1 fix PROPAGATED it to a second surface rather than correcting it. CHANGELOG:36-38 still reads '`compute_design_alignment` shells out to `design-conform` as LEG 1 only in default mode; `compute_design_coherence` calls IT with `mode="rollup"`'. The new ledger bullet at :996-998 repeats the construction: '`compute_design_alignment` shells out to `design-conform` only when `mode != "rollup"` (`qa-gate.sh:15182`), and `compute_design_coherence` calls IT WITH `mode="rollup"` (`:15963`)'. The nearest antecedent of 'it' is `design-conform` in both, and 'compute_design_coherence calls design-conform with mode=rollup' is the exact proposition R2-F1 disproved; `design-conform`'s usage message at :12879 says it 'takes only <task-id>'. The intended antecedent is `compute_design_alignment` -- :15963 is `compute_design_alignment "$mapped_task" "rollup"`, which I read directly.
findings.description: The ledger copy is marginally better than the CHANGELOG's because the inline `:15963` anchor disambiguates for a reader who follows it, and I verified all three anchors in the new bullet resolve exactly (:15182 is `if [ "$mode" != "rollup" ]; then`, :15963 is the alignment call, :16119 is `live_diff_raw=$(bash "$IMPACT_REPORT_SCRIPT" --relativized-changed-files ...)`), plus the CHANGELOG's `:15119-15145` header range, which is correct to the line. Still a low: this is the one sentence in the change set a previous round got factually wrong, and the surviving ambiguity points at the wrong reading, now in two places. Fix: 'calls `compute_design_alignment` with' on both surfaces.

'Reviewed' is the one word of the three accounts that matches none of them, and it displaces 'preserved', which is the operationally load-bearing part. Fix: mirror the CHANGELOG, or say 'implemented and independently verified' (what do5o and LESSONS.md:338 support).

findings.evidence: DP4's closing normative sentence, new in this change set (`git show HEAD:docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md | sed -n '810p'` ends at ~745 chars with '| PROVEN |' -- the entire re-scope is uncommitted), reads: '**No release text may cite this row as evidence that `design-conform` works in a target project. The honest statement is that it has never been observed doing so, in either direction.**' Two sentences earlier the same cell now says 'BOTH REAL-PROJECT OBSERVATIONS OF IT WERE VACUOUS' and the body says 'That happened twice'. Read literally, 'never been observed ... in either direction' says there are no observations; the cell contains two. The phrasing traces to pqoj's operator-ruled comment, which says '"Not established in either direction" is the accurate phrase, not "works"' -- 'not established' does not carry the tension that 'never been observed' does.
findings.description: The operative rule (no release text may cite this row as evidence it works) is clear and correct, and the intended reading (never observed producing a MEANINGFUL answer, in either direction) is recoverable. Low because nothing downstream acts on the second sentence. But it is the same headline-versus-body shape inside one cell that R3-F3 blocked on, in the sentence next door, surviving the fix -- worth closing while the row is open for R4-F1. Fix: restore pqoj's own wording, 'not established in either direction', or 'both observations of it were vacuous, so it has never been observed producing a meaningful answer in either direction'.

Verified: R1-F5's location field IS 'CHANGELOG.md:41-48 and README.md:186-190', so 'the README the finding had explicitly cited' is exact; R2-F1's correction did land in the CHANGELOG while the same change set ADDED the restating bullet to the ledger (hunk `@@ -980,0 +985,21 @@`). findings.description: Two observations, neither blocking. (a) The 'four sentences' detail is wrong by the natural count and the ledger cannot be corrected in place (normalized dedup makes a corrected copy a new entry), so it is worth knowing it is there rather than fixing it. (b) The ledger now carries three entries expressing the same underlying rule in different domains -- :129 (a finding naming one call site; sweep every sibling call site), :304 (fixing the instances on a list versus fixing the class), and :343 (a correction is scoped to a proposition, not the finding's location field). Lessons are criteria-by-reference for the grader, so triplication widens the criteria set without adding a distinct check. :343 earns its place -- it is the only one covering PROSE surfaces and it carries three measured instances -- but a future consolidation pass should know the cluster exists.
